assertions: SyncStepOutcome = 'partial' | 'complete' | 'blocked'.
SyncStepResult = { checkpoint: SyncCheckpoint; progress: { done: number; total?: number; chargedUnits: number }; outcome: SyncStepOutcome }.
SyncStepOptions = { store: OfflineStore; accountId: string; signal: AbortSignal; budget: { maxRecords: 64; maxBytes: number; deadlineMonoMs: number }; checkpoint: SyncCheckpoint | null }.
syncWindowStep(opts: SyncStepOptions): Promise<SyncStepResult>.
syncDeltaStep(opts: SyncStepOptions): Promise<SyncStepResult>.
The winning rollout mode is exactly one of off, observe, or execute.
The feature flag and observe-only classification use one versioned mode contract.
Optional admission is allowed only while criticalActivity === 0.
A 0-to-1 criticalActivity transition aborts optional network I/O at the next checkpoint and preserves the last committed checkpoint.
New optional admission remains closed until the protected Critical lane is quiet.
Optional work never reserves the transport or concurrency capacity required by Critical paths.
Saturated optional load keeps the protected Critical lane independently admissible and measurable.
Optional admission resumes only after five continuous seconds of Critical quiet.
A new Critical event during the quiet window resets the five-second timer.
backgroundWork contractVersion is 1 and snapshot exposes only normalized network cost, power, thermal, storage pressure, and capability booleans.
schedule(jobId, kind, earliestAt, constraints) and cancel(jobId) are optional opportunity hints, not authorization.
Foreground durable-transfer operations accept only scoped token metadata, URL, validator, size/hash, and opaque IDs in memory/keychain scope.
Native-to-WebView events carry opportunity/job IDs and normalized reasons only; TypeScript reloads authoritative policy before work.
Unknown contract versions or capability enum values are denied fail-closed.
A denied or throwing advertised operation narrows capability truth to foregroundReconnectOnly.
No unknown bridge version may silently widen execution or authorization.
Native range reads use GET /mail-attachment/{sha256} and no alternate attachment-download route.
Authorization uses a scoped short-lived transfer token in the Authorization Bearer transport header; the token is never persisted, logged, or placed in a URL.
The route binds immutable SHA-256 identity, strong ETag, byte range, and live authorization on every request.
With feature.connectivity_aware_sync=false and mode=off, syncQoS and backgroundWork are omitted from JSON and HTTP projections.
New routes are absent or return 404 while the feature is OFF.
The pre-V209 and post-V209 OFF artifacts are compared exactly; no background job is admitted.
A pre-V209 binary starts against the ahead V209/V210 additive schema without requiring post-schema fields.
Legacy reducer signatures and OFF behavior remain compatible before the new projection is enabled.
The compatibility proof does not claim post-schema feature parity for an old binary.
Every manifest case has exactly one requirementId, testId, resultId, lane, gate, and retained-artifact binding.
Bindings are exact IDs, never broad substring filters, and unknown or duplicated case IDs fail closed.
The local/native cold, weak, and reconnect baseline is retained only after five complete runs.
No candidate byte, time, concurrency, or resource budget is frozen from fewer than five runs.
The supported-host population contains twenty complete samples before candidate defaults are frozen.
A missing or skipped sample does not satisfy the population threshold.
Decision records expose only requested/effective normalized values, policy/capability source, eligibility, queue class/age, and pause reason.
Account, user, device, job, SSID, carrier, IP, subject, sender, filename, token, URL, and content fields are rejected at every object level.
The receipt records qdisc, isolated database, ports/processes, temp files, and firewall before/after/status actions.
A second cleanup is valid with already_clean for every action and does not claim a new cleanup mutation.
Every failed action includes one exact manual recovery command.
A missing or out-of-range required tool is a failure with its exact tool name and an actionable doctor command.
The verifier never turns missing tooling into a successful skip.
A remaining isolated database, port, process, or qdisc is a failure naming the run ID and cleanup command.
The cleanup receipt remains valid only when every action is cleaned, already_clean, or an explicitly recovered failure.
Duplicate trigger generations coalesce onto one job keyed by coalescing key and never lose a newer trigger.
Each scheduled step applies at most one query/changes page of 64 metadata records within the injected byte/time budget.
An unbounded syncDelta/syncWindow wrapper is refused as scheduled work at coordinator construction.
A 0-to-1 Critical transition aborts optional I/O immediately and preserves the last committed checkpoint.
No server-state cursor advance is committed before the step's local page has committed; a store failure leaves the prior cursor durable.
Planted violations emit exactly 'FAIL CAS-E4I-TRIGGER-STEP-BOUNDS: scheduled step exceeded its bound or advanced an uncommitted cursor' with distinct finite subOracleId cause lines.
A committed atomic batch exposes the page and checkpoint together after reopen; a crash before commit exposes neither.
Migration interruption rolls back the interrupted step and retries cleanly; unknown, ahead and downgrade targets are refused before mutation.

Cross-app handles, ordinary DDL, ATTACH/DETACH/PRAGMA and bare/nested transaction control are refused through exec, query, transactionBatch, migrateStore and execSchemaInit by parsed-keyword engine semantics, never string-prefix matching.
Forged or caller-supplied migration manifests fail digest binding; no runtime registration entry exists.
CAS lease reclaim happens exactly once after expiry and a duplicate terminal result at the same generation is rejected.
The durable job persistence fails closed without the native atomic batch entry; a mock bridge cannot certify real SQLCipher durability, which stays with the native owner's crash harness lane.
The bearer is memory-only for one request lifetime and a restart remints under current authorization; no persisted row retains a bearer or URL.
The destination is constructed from the approved origin and caller URLs must match it exactly; redirects are rejected and never followed, including same-origin redirects.

Confirmed current-authorized 404/410 purges the partial and checkpoint; hidden/ambiguous 404/410 preserves valid encrypted state and pauses admission; stale-generation observations are ignored without purging.
Account change cancels account-scoped work and purges with zero cross-account reuse; revocation drops the bearer and pauses admission.
Critical security work suppresses optional transfer I/O; critical begin/end stays balanced under failure and cancellation.
Planted violations emit exactly 'FAIL CAS-E4I-TRANSFER-LIFECYCLE: transfer lifecycle escaped current authorization or retained a prohibited bearer' with distinct finite subOracleId cause lines.
E4 capability-specific execution and E5 projections consume the same committed, unknown, and paused results through one read seam.
An unknown read maps to idle and never to an invented completion or currentness claim.
A committed paused result keeps its exact pause reason through the shared mapping.
Planted projection disagreement emits exactly 'FAIL CAS-E4I-CONSUMER-PARITY: consumer projection disagreed with the committed execution result' with distinct finite subOracleId cause lines.
An unknown coordinator read maps to idle through the shared E4-I seam and is never displayed as a completion or currentness.
neverSynced displays the stable never_synced key ("Not synced on this device") and unknown the distinct unknown key ("Sync status unavailable"); the two never collapse.
A committed complete result is idle and a committed paused result keeps its exact reason through the same mapping.
Planted violations emit exactly "FAIL CAS-E5-NEVER-UNKNOWN: E5 status invented a completion or mislabeled unknown freshness" with distinct finite subOracleId cause lines.
Terminal transfer expiry displays the download_expired key ("Download expired") with retry (newly authorized restart) and never Open/Save.
Authorized content-unavailable classification displays the content_unavailable key ("Attachment unavailable") with no retry action.
Integrity failure displays the verification_failed key ("Verification failed") without Open/Save and is the only alert-worthy terminal.
Every contract PauseReason maps to a distinct verbatim key and travels unchanged into the matching transfer row state.
Planted violations emit exactly "FAIL CAS-E5-TRANSFER-TERMINALS: transfer terminal display offered a prohibited action" with distinct finite subOracleId cause lines.
Save all keeps independent child identities and reports completed/total plus failed/cancelled/expired child counts.
Partial completion never reports success: allComplete is true only when every requested child is complete.
Unknown child sizes make aggregate progress genuinely indeterminate (bytes.total absent).
Planted violations emit exactly "FAIL CAS-E5-SAVE-ALL-PARTIAL: save-all group misreported partial progress as success" with distinct finite subOracleId cause lines.
Cancel stops exactly the unfinished children and preserves every completed download.
Group retry selects only eligible failed children (recoverable errors and newly authorized expired restarts), never unavailable, cancelled, or verification-failed children.
Component unmount does not cancel the group: the controller lives outside the card.
Planted violations emit exactly "FAIL CAS-E5-SAVE-ALL-CANCEL-RETRY: save-all cancel/retry escaped the eligible-child contract" with distinct finite subOracleId cause lines.
One accessible group announcement replaces the per-child burst: a settled batch of three children produces exactly one announcement.
Transfer progress announces phase changes and 10% thresholds only; intra-band movement never announces.
Planted violations emit exactly "FAIL CAS-E5-GROUP-ANNOUNCER: group announcer burst or announced per-chunk noise" with distinct finite subOracleId cause lines.
A failed save preserves the user drafts verbatim, leaves the acknowledged effective state untouched, and surfaces a remedy — it never reports success.
Only the authoritative server response updates the acknowledged state; the client never recomputes precedence.
Planted violations emit exactly "FAIL CAS-E5-PREFERENCE-SAVE-FAILURE: preference save failure reported success or lost drafts" with distinct finite subOracleId cause lines.
A pending save refuses duplicate submission without disturbing the in-flight request.
Planted violations emit exactly "FAIL CAS-E5-PREFERENCE-DOUBLE-SUBMIT: a second preference submission escaped the pending guard" with distinct finite subOracleId cause lines.
An account/device change invalidates the pending response: the in-flight reply resolves to a stale-binding refusal and can never update the new binding.
The previous binding's acknowledged values and drafts never carry across; the new binding starts from defaults.
Planted violations emit exactly "FAIL CAS-E5-PREFERENCE-ACCOUNT-RACE: a pending preference response survived an account change" with distinct finite subOracleId cause lines.
Every preview response binds the selected target and the request generation: an old-generation response cannot replace a newer selection.
A payload whose device identity does not match the selected target is refused before display.
Planted violations emit exactly "FAIL CAS-E5-PREVIEW-TARGET-RACE: a stale preview response replaced a newer selection" with distinct finite subOracleId cause lines.
Failed refreshes label retained facts stale; unavailable and unauthorized are distinct honest states, never displayed as current.
Malformed or ahead-version envelopes fail closed; a disabled winning policy stays visible with its source facts.
Planted violations emit exactly "FAIL CAS-E5-PREVIEW-UNAVAILABLE: preview failure was displayed as success or current facts" with distinct finite subOracleId cause lines.

The four crossed combinations (refresh Never/attachments permitted, refresh permitted/attachments Never, policy/metered narrowing, Background sync Off with permissive stored preferences) each explain actual admission from server-resolved values.
The explanation never promises "all network disabled": background-off still allows explicit actions, and refresh Never never implies attachment Never.
Wire enums stay scoped: any for refresh, always for attachments.
Planted violations emit exactly "FAIL CAS-E5-CROSSED-NETWORK-ATTACHMENT: crossed settings explanation promised more than actual admission" with distinct finite subOracleId cause lines.

The versioned E6 comparison profile document exists, parses, and validates: freeze semantics, measurement protocol (20 pairs, 120 s warmup, 300 s measurement, 1,000 observations per Critical class per run, nearest-rank percentiles, 10,000 paired bootstrap resamples, upper one-sided 95% bound), and the section 8 regression ceilings are pinned exactly.

Every platform is explicitly selected (a frozen profile entry binding host/shell/tool builds, corpus/cache, clients, Critical request classes/mix, optional saturation, network faults, process metric boundaries, clocks and seeds) or explicitly unselected with a freeze-before-any-results-qualify rule; selection is never inferred.

The profile states that results qualify only their exact frozen profile and that post-result workload/metric/seed/stopping changes are prohibited; any binding change requires a new profileVersion and manifest rebinding.
A manifest case that binds requiredProfiles fails closed unless every referenced profile exists in the document with status frozen.
Each claimed Critical class records at least 1,000 completed observations per run; a class below the floor cannot make any claim.
Insufficient observations mean unavailable claims, never interpolated or borrowed evidence from another profile or run.
The run binds exactly the frozen profile selected in requiredProfiles; results qualify only that profile.
At least 20 independent flag-OFF versus execute pairs run with identical workloads and randomized order, each with a two-minute warmup and five-minute measurement window.

Nearest-rank p95/p99 with 10,000 seeded paired-bootstrap resamples use the upper one-sided 95% bound for each existing relative and absolute regression ceiling; a breach fails E6 rather than being explained away.
A changed workload, metric, seed, or stopping rule after results exist requires a new profileVersion and a new separately identified run; results never transfer across profiles.
Failures and timeouts are reported separately from completed observations for every run and class.
A latency improvement obtained by dropping failures cannot pass: all attempts are retained and every comparison includes the failed attempts.
No post-result change to the attempt population, workload, metric, seed, or stopping rule is permitted inside a frozen profile run.

Cross-process contention under saturated optional load keeps Critical p95 within 5% and 50 ms, p99 within 10% and 100 ms, and peak process CPU/RSS within 10% of the paired flag-OFF run; both limits of each pair apply.
The protected Critical lane stays independently admissible and measurable while optional work saturates the declared concurrency limits.
High-cardinality job/account IDs and content never enter the recorded metrics.

cases.command: cd mailserver/webmail && npx vitest run src/lib/offline/e6Diagnostics.test.ts -t CAS-E6-DIAGNOSTIC-BOUNDS

assertions: The per-device diagnostics store holds at most 1,000 records and 1 MiB; whenever any limit is hit the oldest records are evicted until all limits hold.
Records expire after seven days; an already-expired append is never served.
One export is at most 1 MiB and always carries exact omitted-count metadata (exported + omitted === stored).
The bounds are a restriction enforced at the only entry points, not a flag-gated feature.

cases.command: cd mailserver/webmail && npx vitest run src/lib/offline/e6Diagnostics.test.ts -t CAS-E6-EXPORTER-FAILURE

assertions: An exporter failure (sync throw or rejection) is returned as a failed outcome and never propagates into a mail path.
An export is exactly one attempt; no retry queue exists, so repeated failures cannot grow any backlog.
Mail paths keep working across exporter failures: appends and exports remain available afterwards.

cases.command: cd mailserver/webmail && npx vitest run src/lib/offline/e6Diagnostics.test.ts -t CAS-E6-METRIC-LABEL-ALLOWLIST

assertions: Metric labels are exactly the finite plan section 8 enum (time-to-cached-list through critical-p99); unknown labels such as job or account identifiers are rejected, never stored.
Dimension values are the existing finite work-contract enums: pause-reason requires a PauseReason and queue-age requires an OptionalWorkClass; both are forbidden on every other metric.
Malformed values, kinds, timestamps, extra fields, and ahead schema versions fail closed.

cases.command: cd mailserver/webmail && npx vitest run src/lib/offline/e6Diagnostics.test.ts -t CAS-E6-SMALL-COHORT-SUPPRESSION

assertions: A cross-user bucket releases only with at least 10 DISTINCT authorized contributors; below the threshold it is suppressed as below-minimum-cohort.
One unauthorized contribution suppresses its whole bucket (unavailable proof means omit), even when every other contributor is authorized.
Contributor tokens are used only to count distinctness and never appear in any released bucket: released envelopes carry counts and sums only, never identity telemetry.
Bucket keys are bounded: unknown metrics, unknown dimension values, and dimensions on non-dimensional metrics are malformed and suppressed.

The versioned E7 useful-outcome contract document exists, parses, and validates: contractId, frozenAtUtc, freeze semantics, capability scoping, outcome bindings, the incomplete-outcome rule, the usefulness-not-safety-only distinction, the expansion rule, and the pilot scope are pinned exactly.
Every bound outcome name is a verbatim name from the plan's Metrics and initial success criteria list; an outcome name absent from that list is rejected fail-closed.
At least one primary foreground/reconnect usefulness outcome is bound, and every outcome names the E4-I/E5 capabilities it applies to.

A pilot may not begin while any required outcome field (threshold, sample rule, missing-data rule, cohort, observation window, denominator, OFF comparator) is unspecified; all outcome evidence stays planned until the separately gated pilot run.
Usefulness outcomes never substitute for the E6 safety/SLO gates; the contract records usefulnessOutcomesSubstituteForSafetyGates=false fail-closed.
E6 Critical-path regression ceilings, resource budgets, and security/privacy gates remain nonwaivable; missing usefulness evidence holds only the affected expansion or claim.
Metrics that stay E6-owned (foreground latency/CPU contention under background work) are not rebranded as pilot usefulness outcomes.
A pilot with unspecified required outcome fields cannot begin: pilotMayNotBeginWithUnspecifiedFields=true fails closed.
Every bound outcome carries threshold, sample-rule, and missing-data-rule fields, and the pilot scope carries cohort, observation-window, denominator, and OFF-comparator fields.
A baseline-justified threshold carries its finite numeric value and basis; pending thresholds stay honestly pending-q0-baseline instead of a fabricated number.
The retained pilot decision precedes expansion, and scope fields that are planned-until-pilot-admission keep the begin-gate engaged.
Every outcome binding names a non-empty set of E4-I/E5 capabilities from the contract's capability registry; unscoped outcomes and unknown capabilities fail closed.
The pilot scope binds frozen selected profiles from the E6 profile document; unknown or unfrozen profile IDs fail closed.
Attachment prefetch stays excluded from pilot admission unless explicitly widened, and results qualify only their exact frozen profile.

The all profile selection is a local deterministic aggregate, not E7 release readiness: the frozen E6 profile document keeps platform selection explicit — every platform is a frozen selected profile or explicitly unselected with freeze-before-any-results-qualify — and results qualify only their exact frozen profile, never an inferred all.

The sustained selected-profile runtime evidence cases (CAS-E6-CRITICAL-SAMPLE-FLOOR, CAS-E6-PAIRED-REGRESSION, CAS-E6-FAILED-REQUEST-ACCOUNTING, CAS-E6-CROSSPROCESS-CRITICAL-SATURATION) stay present, requiredState required, and bound to non-empty frozen requiredProfiles; removing or downgrading one fails closed because the local aggregate cannot substitute for selected-profile runtime evidence.

A case bound to requiredProfiles can never carry the local manifest-checker command as its runtime evidence, and all is rejected as a pseudo-profile binding: release readiness requires the selected-profile runtime evidence.

Capability-scoped outcomes bind only to capability evidence that exists: the frozen contract's capabilityScoping stays fail-closed — unscoped outcomes prohibited, non-empty capability sets from the registry, unknown capabilities rejected.
Every pilot-admitted capability's owning unit (E4-I/E5) has at least one actual capability evidence binding in the manifest evidence registry; an admitted-without-evidence capability fails closed.

A primary-usefulness outcome must bind at least one pilot-admitted capability from the registry: a capability that is not admitted to the pilot (attachment-prefetch) cannot inherit a usefulness claim.
